6-8.title: Life in a Pond Ecosystem
6-8.titleEs: La vida en el ecosistema de un estanque

prompts.prompt: Explain how removing the algae would affect the fish in the pond.

needs.text: States the effect on the fish
Gives the cause, using words like because or so
Uses science ideas such as producers or the food chain
Tells what algae look like
Tells how algae and fish are alike and different

answers.text: Algae are tiny green organisms that float near the surface. They can make the water look cloudy.
Algae and fish both live in the pond, but algae make their own food while fish must eat other organisms.

Removing the algae would hurt the fish because algae are producers at the base of the food chain. Small animals like insect larvae eat algae, and fish eat those animals. With less food moving up the chain, the fish population would likely shrink.

prompts.why: Answer C states the effect and explains the cause through the food chain. A describes algae, and B compares algae and fish.

prompts.prompt: How are producers and consumers in the pond alike and different?

needs.text: Gives at least one way they are alike
Gives at least one way they are different
Uses examples of each from the pond
Explains only why producers matter
Lists the order of a food chain

answers.text: Producers and consumers are both living things that need energy to survive. They are different because producers, like pond plants, make their own food from sunlight, while consumers, like frogs, must eat other organisms.
Producers are important because they make food from sunlight. Without them, the pond would have no energy.
First the sun shines on the plants. Then insects eat the plants, and frogs eat the insects.

prompts.why: Answer A gives a likeness and a difference with examples. B explains only producers, and C puts a food chain in order.

prompts.prompt: Put in order the steps of energy flow in this food chain: sun, algae, snail, fish, heron.

needs.text: Starts at the beginning and goes to the end
Uses transition words like next, then, and finally
Says which living thing is most important
Tells what one animal looks like

answers.text: The heron is the most important animal in the pond because it is at the top of the food chain. It keeps the fish population in check.
Energy starts with the sun. Next, algae use sunlight to make food. Then a snail eats the algae, a fish eats the snail, and finally a heron eats the fish.
A heron is a tall gray bird with long legs and a sharp beak. It stands very still in shallow water.

prompts.why: Answer B follows the energy from the sun to the heron in order. A argues for one animal, and C describes the heron.

prompts.prompt: Describe the three branches of the United States government.

needs.text: Names all three branches
Gives details about who or what is in each branch

answers.text: The founders created three branches because they did not want one group to hold too much power.
The legislative branch is the most important because it writes the laws that everyone must follow.

The legislative branch is Congress, which has the Senate and the House of Representatives. The executive branch is led by the president. The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

prompts.why: Answer C names each branch and gives details about it. A explains why, and B argues for one branch.

I think the delegates should have finished faster. Meeting all summer was too long, and people back home were waiting.

6-8.title: Smoothie Stand Ratios
6-8.titleEs: Razones en el puesto de licuados

prompts.prompt: The recipe uses 2 cups of strawberries for every 3 cups of yogurt. Explain why 4 cups of strawberries and 6 cups of yogurt make the same flavor.

needs.text: Gives the math reason, using because or so
Shows how the two ratios are equivalent
Lists the steps for making the smoothie
Tells how the smoothie looks and tastes

answers.text: First, pour 4 cups of strawberries into the blender. Then add 6 cups of yogurt and blend until smooth.
The smoothie is thick and pink, and it tastes sweet with a little tang.
It makes the same flavor because both amounts were doubled. 2 times 2 is 4, and 3 times 2 is 6, so the ratio 4 to 6 is equivalent to 2 to 3. The strawberries and yogurt stay in the same balance.

prompts.why: Answer C gives the math reason and shows the ratios are equivalent. A gives steps, and B describes the smoothie.

prompts.prompt: Recipe A uses 1 cup of mango for every 2 cups of milk. Recipe B uses 3 cups of mango for every 4 cups of milk. Compare the two recipes.

needs.text: Tells how the recipes are alike
Tells how the recipes are different, using the ratios
Describes only one recipe
Says which recipe is healthier

answers.text: Recipe B is a bright orange smoothie made with 3 cups of mango and 4 cups of milk. It is thick and cold.

Both recipes use only mango and milk. Recipe A has a ratio of 1 to 2, which equals 2 to 4, so it uses less mango for 4 cups of milk than Recipe B, which is 3 to 4. Recipe B will taste more like mango.
Recipe A is better because it is healthier, and people should drink more milk.

prompts.why: Answer B tells how the recipes are alike and uses equivalent ratios to show how they differ. A describes one recipe, and C argues for one.

prompts.prompt: Use the recipe with 2 cups of strawberries for every 3 cups of yogurt. Tell the steps in order to find how much yogurt is needed for 10 cups of strawberries.

needs.text: Gives each step of the math from start to finish
Uses order words like first, next, and then
Ends with the answer to the question
Gives an opinion about the recipe
Explains why ratios are useful

answers.text: First, write the ratio of strawberries to yogurt as 2 to 3. Next, find what 2 is multiplied by to get 10, which is 5. Then multiply 3 by 5 to get 15. So 10 cups of strawberries need 15 cups of yogurt.
I think the stand should use less yogurt, because the strawberries are the best part of the smoothie.
Ratios are useful because they help cooks make bigger batches that still taste right.

prompts.why: Answer A gives the math steps in order and ends with the answer. B gives an opinion, and C explains why ratios matter.
